title: National AML/CFT Strategy and FATF Mutual Evaluations
summary: A ten-module programme helping government, FIU and law enforcement officials build an effective national AML/CFT system and prepare for FATF mutual evaluations.
intro: This training programme equips government, FIU and law enforcement officials to build an effective national AML/CFT system: assessing risk, coordinating agencies, strengthening the legal framework and preparing for, and responding to, a FATF mutual evaluation.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give the officials who lead and deliver a country's AML/CFT regime a practical understanding of the FATF standards, the assessment methodology and what effectiveness really means. Participants leave able to lead a national risk assessment, coordinate a whole-of-government response, prepare a credible mutual evaluation submission and design an action plan to address deficiencies or exit increased monitoring.
sections.What It Covers: The FATF standards and assessment methodology, national risk assessment, national strategy and coordination bodies, the legal and institutional framework, beneficial ownership transparency and registers, the FIU and financial intelligence, investigation, prosecution and confiscation, supervision and preventive measures, international cooperation, preparing for a mutual evaluation, and grey-list exit action plans.
Intended Audience: Officials in finance, justice and interior ministries who lead national AML/CFT policy and coordination
FIU directors and analysts, financial investigators, prosecutors and asset recovery officials
Members and secretariats of national AML/CFT coordination committees and mutual evaluation teams
Learning Objectives: Explain the FATF Recommendations, the immediate outcomes and how effectiveness is assessed
Lead or contribute to a national money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment
Design national coordination arrangements and a risk-based AML/CFT strategy
Assess the legal framework, beneficial ownership transparency and operational effectiveness
Prepare evidence, case studies and statistics for a mutual evaluation
Develop an action plan to address deficiencies and exit increased monitoring
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as an intensive programme over three to four days or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing with country case studies and practical exercises, including a mock evaluation, and modules can be selected or tailored to the country's evaluation timetable.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT policy, financial intelligence or law enforcement is helpful. No prior involvement in a mutual evaluation is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2012, updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
FATF (2013, updated), Methodology for Assessing Technical Compliance with the FATF Recommendations and the Effectiveness of AML/CFT Systems
FATF (2013), National Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment
FATF (2023), Guidance on Beneficial Ownership of Legal Persons

modules.title: The FATF Standards and the Global Network
modules.summary: How the FATF and its regional bodies work, what the 40 Recommendations require, and why a country's AML/CFT performance matters for its financial sector, reputation and economy.
objectives: Describe the FATF, FATF-style regional bodies and the global network
Summarise the structure and main requirements of the FATF Recommendations
Explain the economic and reputational consequences of weak AML/CFT systems
syllabus: The FATF, regional bodies and observer organisations
The 40 Recommendations: policy, criminal justice, preventive and transparency measures
Proliferation financing and targeted financial sanctions
De-risking, correspondent banking and the cost of listing

modules.title: Technical Compliance and Effectiveness: The Methodology
modules.summary: How assessors rate technical compliance and effectiveness, what the immediate outcomes test, and the procedures and timeline of the current round of mutual evaluations.
objectives: Distinguish technical compliance ratings from effectiveness ratings
Explain the immediate outcomes and the core issues assessors examine
Describe the mutual evaluation process, follow-up and listing triggers
syllabus: Technical compliance criteria and ratings
The immediate outcomes, core issues and levels of effectiveness
Evaluation procedures: questionnaires, on-site visit and plenary
Follow-up, enhanced follow-up and the listing process

modules.title: National Risk Assessment
modules.summary: How to plan, conduct and use a national assessment of money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing risks, including sectoral and thematic assessments.
objectives: Design the scope, methodology and governance of a national risk assessment
Gather and analyse threat, vulnerability and consequence data
Translate risk findings into policy priorities and resource allocation
syllabus: Methodologies, data sources and private sector input
Threats, vulnerabilities and consequences by sector and product
Sectoral assessments: legal persons, virtual assets and non-profit organisations
Communicating results and keeping the assessment current

modules.title: National Strategy, Coordination and Legal Framework
modules.summary: How to turn risk findings into a national AML/CFT strategy, design an effective coordination body, and ensure the legal and institutional framework meets the standards.
objectives: Design a national AML/CFT strategy linked to the risk assessment
Establish coordination mechanisms with clear mandates and accountability
Assess gaps in criminal, preventive and administrative legislation
syllabus: Strategy design: priorities, owners, resources and milestones
National coordination committees: membership, mandate and secretariat
Criminalisation of money laundering and terrorist financing
Domestic cooperation, information sharing and data protection

modules.title: Beneficial Ownership Transparency and Registers
modules.summary: Why opaque legal persons and arrangements are a core vulnerability, the FATF requirements on beneficial ownership, and the policy choices in designing and operating registers.
objectives: Explain the FATF requirements for legal persons and legal arrangements
Evaluate register models, verification and access arrangements
Assess whether competent authorities obtain accurate information in a timely way
syllabus: Recommendations 24 and 25 and the multi-pronged approach
Register design: scope, thresholds, verification and sanctions
Access for authorities, obliged entities and the public
Trusts, nominees, bearer shares and foreign legal persons

modules.title: Financial Intelligence and the FIU
modules.summary: The role of the national FIU in receiving, analysing and disseminating financial intelligence, and how its effectiveness is measured and demonstrated to assessors.
objectives: Describe the FIU's core functions, independence and resources
Assess the quality and use of suspicious transaction reports and FIU disseminations
Demonstrate the use of financial intelligence by law enforcement
syllabus: FIU models, autonomy and access to information
Reporting quality, feedback and public-private partnerships
Operational and strategic analysis products
Statistics and case studies that evidence effectiveness

modules.title: Investigation, Prosecution and Confiscation
modules.summary: How law enforcement, prosecutors and asset recovery bodies pursue money laundering, terrorist financing and the proceeds of crime, and what assessors expect to see in results.
objectives: Assess whether investigations and prosecutions match the risk profile
Evaluate confiscation, asset recovery and asset management arrangements
Identify practical obstacles in parallel financial investigations
syllabus: Parallel financial investigations and stand-alone money laundering cases
Prosecution strategies, sentencing and alternative measures
Freezing, seizure, confiscation and non-conviction based forfeiture
Terrorist financing investigations and targeted financial sanctions

modules.title: Supervision, Preventive Measures and International Cooperation
modules.summary: How financial and non-financial sectors are supervised for AML/CFT, the preventive measures they apply, and how the country cooperates with foreign counterparts.
objectives: Assess risk-based supervision of financial institutions, DNFBPs and VASPs
Explain the preventive measures obliged entities must apply
Evaluate mutual legal assistance, extradition and informal cooperation
syllabus: Supervisory coverage, risk-based supervision and sanctions
Customer due diligence, monitoring and reporting obligations
Lawyers, accountants, real estate, casinos and virtual asset providers
Mutual legal assistance, extradition and FIU-to-FIU exchange

modules.title: Preparing for a Mutual Evaluation
modules.summary: Practical preparation for an assessment: organising the national team, assembling evidence, writing the technical compliance and effectiveness submissions, and managing the on-site visit and plenary.
objectives: Organise a national evaluation team, timetable and governance
Build a compelling evidence base of statistics and case studies
Prepare officials for on-site interviews and plenary discussion
syllabus: Gap analysis and a mock evaluation
Statistics, case studies and evidence of outcomes
Drafting the technical compliance and effectiveness submissions
On-site interviews, draft report review and plenary negotiation

modules.title: Responding to Findings and Exiting Increased Monitoring
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining how to respond to evaluation findings, agree and deliver an action plan under increased monitoring, and sustain effectiveness after exit.
objectives: Prioritise recommended actions and allocate ownership and resources
Design and deliver an action plan that meets increased monitoring deadlines
Sustain reforms and prepare for follow-up assessments
syllabus: Prioritising recommended actions by impact and feasibility
Increased monitoring: action plans, reporting and on-site verification
Political leadership, resourcing and communication with industry
Workshop: a national action plan to address deficiencies

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Typologies, Tracing and Controls
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping supervisors, FIU analysts and investigators to recognise crypto-asset crime typologies, trace funds on-chain and assess service providers' controls.

related.title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.

related.title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.

related.title: Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime Investigations
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud, money mules and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to recover funds.

related.title: Prosecuting Financial Crime: Evidence, Experts and the Courtroom
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases, from charge and evidence to sentencing and confiscation.
